new_camps.name: Chopping Block ridge camp
new_camps.why: Flat spots on the ridge crest below the Chopping Block, above the basin; the climb starts from here, but the nearest running water takes some effort to reach.
new_camps.water: Running water is a descent away from the ridge; carry a supply up.
new_camps.permit: Overnight camping in the Pickets needs a backcountry permit from North Cascades National Park.
new_camps.notes: Parties camp on the crest after crossing the roughly 6,400 ft saddle. It is exposed and dry but puts the Twin Needles, Ottohorn and Himmelhorn within reach.

plan_conflict: No camp is on file; the plan's day 1 ends at a col near the Chopping Block, which is where parties sleep before the day-2 climb.

camps.name: Crescent Creek Basin camp
camps.why: Basin camp under the western peaks with flat heather spots and water; it puts the climb a short walk from the tent, at the price of crossing the Barrier on the way in.

camps.name: Terror Basin camp
camps.why: Flat gravel camp with water, a day's approach in. Parties heading to the Crescent Creek side stop here first; it is not the camp these climbs start from.

camps.name: Chopping Block saddle camp (above Crescent Creek Basin)
camps.why: Exposed dry perch on the crest above the basin with a grandstand view; it saves the descent into the basin, but you carry water, so most parties prefer the basin.

camps.name: Goodell Creek Campground, roadhead staging
camps.why: Car camping the night before; it gains nothing on the approach but lets you start the long climb rested and in daylight, with bear boxes for food.

camps.name: Old Goodell Creek roadbed near the Terror Creek crossing
camps.why: Flat-ish ground on the old road about four miles in; a late start from the car can end day one here, but it leaves the whole steep Barrier climb for the morning.

camps.name: Stump Hollow bench
camps.why: Open heather benches at timberline give the first comfortable tent sites above the brush; stopping here splits the approach and sets up the saddle crossing next morning.

camps.name: High bivouacs at the western end of the crest
camps.why: Improvised bivouacs high on the crest for parties linking the western summits; not a normal night for a standard out-and-back trip, and quality varies.
